content.title: About
content.content: Baked beans, reduced sodium are canned beans cooked in a savory tomato sauce with less added salt. They retain the classic sweet‑savory flavor while being suitable for those watching their sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Baked beans became popular in the United States in the early 20th century as a quick, hearty meal for workers.
The reduced‑sodium version uses spices and tomato paste to replace much of the salt.
One 425 g package provides about 1.5 g of protein and 5 g of dietary fiber.
Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, an antioxidant linked to heart health.
Glass jars preserve flavor better than metal cans.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Beans supply a complete set of essential amino acids, beneficial for vegetarians and athletes.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports regular bowel movements and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt helps maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals aid in hemoglobin formation and muscle function.

items.title: Lycopene and other antioxidants
items.content: The tomato base provides lycopene, which protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Tomato sauce can contain added sugar; people with diabetes should account for it.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive persons.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands may include preservatives such as sodium benzoate.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve baked beans as a side dish, add them to chili, casseroles, salads, or use as a filling for tortillas. They heat quickly in the microwave or on the stovetop.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened jar in a cool, dry place. After opening, store in the refrigerator in an airtight container and consume within 5 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
